from ./Lod import Lod

export anchor Performance:
    description:
        The cost of the tree system is measured in the running game, not
        guessed, so it can be compared with the hand-made trees it replaced.

    counters:
        - A tree stats overlay, shown with the @{Lod.debugView} toggle, reports per frame the number of trees drawn at each level and in a fade, the triangles and draw calls of the tree passes, shadow passes included, and the GPU time of the tree main pass and tree shadow pass on their own.
        - It also reports the CPU time of level selection and fade updates per frame.
        - At stage load it records the time spent deriving, meshing and baking variants, how many came from the disk cache, and the GPU and disk memory the variants use.

    benchmark:
        - A benchmark runs a fixed camera path along a stage with the procedural trees and reports the average, 1% low and worst frame time, the tree GPU time and the stage load time.
        - It can run the same path with trees turned off, so the trees' own cost is the difference between the two runs.
        - Results are written to a file with the stage, graphics quality setting, resolution and GPU, so runs can be compared.

    hotspots:
        - Alpha-tested foliage overdraw near the camera, made larger by the 120 m full-detail distance.
        - The two levels drawn together during a fade.
        - Shadow casters, drawn again for each cascade.
        - Stage load on a cold cache, when every variant and impostor is generated.

from ./Foliage import Foliage
from ./Grammar import Grammar
from ./Lod import Lod
from ./Placement import Placement
from ./Species import Species

export anchor ProceduralTrees:
    description:
        Every tree in the rally game is generated procedurally from a
        parametric, stochastic, bracketed L-system. The hand-made tree
        assets the game used before are replaced and no longer loaded or
        placed anywhere. One generated branch skeleton per tree variant is
        the single source for every level of detail, for its foliage, its
        wind animation and its collision, so all of them agree with each
        other.

    pipeline:
        - The species definition and a seed are expanded by the grammar into a symbol string (@{Grammar}).
        - A turtle interprets the string into a branch skeleton and leaf attachment points.
        - The skeleton is meshed into every LOD, foliage cards are built on its leaf points, and the impostor is baked from the full-detail tree (@{Lod}, @{Foliage}).
        - Trees are placed along the stage and drawn as instances of a small pool of variants per species (@{Placement}).

    species: Tree kinds are data, not code; see @{Species}.

    integration:
        - The tree system is built inside the game's existing codebase, in its language, on its renderer, and reads its stage data, collision, camera and graphics quality settings. It adds no second engine or renderer.
        - The tree system is one module with stages for grammar, skeleton, meshing, impostor baking, placement and drawing, in that order. Each stage only reads the output of the stages before it.
        - Grammar derivation and skeleton building are pure functions of the species and the seed, with no engine dependency, so they can be unit tested on their own.
        - The old tree assets and the code that loaded and placed them are removed, not left behind a switch.

    goals:
        - LOD changes are not visible as pops: the silhouette, crown volume, colour and lighting of a tree stay continuous while it changes level.
        - Foliage reads as clustered leaves on real branches, lit from both sides and moving in the wind, not as flat cards stuck on a trunk.
        - The same stage always grows the same trees, on every machine and in every replay.

# Performance

## Description

The cost of the tree system is measured in the running game, not guessed. The hand-made trees are gone, so the cost is measured against the same stage with no trees.

## Counters

- A tree stats overlay, shown with the [Lod.debugView](./Lod.md#debug-view) toggle, reports per frame the number of trees drawn at each level and in a fade, the triangles and draw calls of the tree passes, shadow passes included, and the GPU time of the tree main pass and tree shadow pass on their own.
- It also reports the CPU time of level selection and fade updates per frame.
- At stage load it records the time spent deriving, meshing and baking variants, how many came from the disk cache, and the GPU and disk memory the variants use.

## Benchmark

- A benchmark runs a fixed camera path along a stage with the procedural trees and reports the average, 1% low and worst frame time, the tree GPU time and the stage load time.
- It can run the same path with trees turned off, so the trees' own cost is the difference between the two runs.
- Results are written to a file with the stage, graphics quality setting, resolution and GPU, so runs can be compared.

## Hotspots

- Alpha-tested foliage overdraw near the camera, made larger by the 120 m full-detail distance.
- The two levels drawn together during a fade.
- Shadow casters, drawn again for each cascade.
- Stage load on a cold cache, when every variant and impostor is generated.
- What all of this costs at load and per frame is measured in the game ([Performance](./Performance.md#performance)).

content.text:
I can't give you a measured number yet, because there's still no game code in `src/` to profile. So I've added measurement tools to the spec, and the code step will build them so the real cost can be read in game. Until then, this is my estimate from what the spec requires.

**Per frame, the cost is mostly foliage and shadows, not the L-system:**
- **Leaf overdraw near the camera** is the biggest cost. Every tree within 120 m draws at full detail, and leaf cards are layered and alpha-tested. Moving the full-detail distance out last time made this much larger. Expect the tree passes to use a large share of GPU time on dense forest stages.
- **Shadows** are probably the second biggest. Shadow casters are drawn again for each cascade, and foliage dominates them too.
- **Fades** are minor. Both levels draw only for 0.3 s while a tree changes level.
- **Wind** runs on the GPU from data baked into the vertices, so it costs almost nothing on the CPU.
- **Draw calls** stay low: about 3 species × 8 variants × 4 levels, so 100 batches or fewer in total.
- **The L-system itself** costs nothing per frame. Trees are generated at stage load, off the main thread.

**At load:** the first run of a stage generates every variant and impostor, which could take seconds. After that, variants come from the disk cache and loading should cost little extra.

**What I added to the spec:**
- **`spec/trees/Performance.pi`** (new anchor `Performance`):
  - **Counters:** a tree stats overlay, shown with the LOD debug toggle. Each frame it shows how many trees are at each level and how many are fading, plus triangles, draw calls, the tree pass's GPU time and the tree shadow pass's GPU time. It also shows the CPU time spent picking levels and updating fades. At stage load it records generation time, how many variants came from the cache, and GPU and disk memory.
  - **Benchmark:** a fixed camera path along a stage, run with trees and then without. The difference is the cost of the trees. It reports average, 1% low and worst frame time, tree GPU time and load time, and writes them to a file together with the stage, quality setting, resolution and GPU.
  - **Hotspots:** the four costs above (leaf overdraw, fades, shadow cascades, first-run loading) are named so the work on them is aimed at the right places.
- **`spec/trees/ProceduralTrees.pi`:** a `pipeline` step now links to `Performance`.

`piton check` and `piton build` both pass.

**Anchors the code should follow:** `Performance.counters` and `Performance.benchmark` in `.claude/reference/trees/Performance.md`, with the overlay shown through `Lod.debugView`. Once the code step has run the benchmark, its results file answers your question.
